rows.question: My Unlimited Edition copy of Word of Command reads "You may look at opponent's hand and choose any card opponent can legally play using mana from his or her mana pool or lands. rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: Your Unlimited Edition copy is governed by the current Oracle text, which no longer limits you to a card the opponent could legally play and instead lets you look at target opponent's hand, choose a card from it, and control that player until Word of Command finishes resolving.
Missing: None
Why: The printed Unlimited wording and the current Oracle wording differ in three material ways: the current text targets the opponent and lets you choose any card from their hand rather than only one they could pay for; it grants you control of that player for the duration instead of saying "you make all the decisions it calls for"; and it spells out a mana-ability restriction plus control of the player while a chosen spell resolves. The old "may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand" sentence is gone from the card text, but the 2011 rulings state that the opponent still cannot counter Word of Command after letting you look at their hand. I did not retrieve CR 108.1, so I do not cite it.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text for Word of Command, which is the wording a card is played with; the printed Unlimited Edition wording is superseded.
Quote [printed, Unlimited Edition, complete]: "You may look at opponent's hand and choose any card opponent can legally play using mana from his or her mana pool or lands. Opponent must play this card immediately; you make all the decisions it calls for. This spell may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand."
Quote [current Oracle text, complete]: "Look at target opponent's hand and choose a card from it. You control that player until Word of Command finishes resolving. The player plays that card if able. While doing so, the player can activate mana abilities only if they're from lands that player controls and only if mana they produce is spent to activate other mana abilities of lands the player controls and/or to play that card. If the chosen card is cast as a spell, you control the player while that spell is resolving."
Quote [ruling 2011-01-01, complete]: "Since this spell is an instant, your opponent gets a chance to respond to it as normal. Once this spell resolves, you look at your opponent's hand and choose a card. Note that it is common practice to respond to Word of Command by using up any spells or mana you have prior to letting it resolve."
Quote [ruling 2011-01-01, complete]: "Your opponent can't counter the Word of Command after letting you look at their hand, but they can attempt to counter the spell you force them to cast."
Quote [ruling 2011-01-01, complete]: "You must order your opponent to play the chosen card if it is possible to do so."
Quote [ruling 2011-01-01, complete]: "You may Command your opponent to play a land (if they have not already done so this turn)."
Rules: CR 604.6, CR 702.144a (both retrieved; neither bears on this question)
Conflict: The printed Unlimited text says the chosen card must be one the opponent can legally play using their mana pool or lands, and that you make all decisions; the current Oracle text drops the legality restriction on the choice, gives you control of the player instead of making decisions, and restricts which mana abilities the player may activate. The Oracle text wins. The printed "may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand" sentence is absent from the Oracle text but is preserved as a ruling rather than as card text.
